name: D4Sign
tagline: Brazilian electronic signature platform for sending, signing and archiving documents with audit trails and ICP-Brasil certificate support.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanics of e-signature are embarrassingly simple: render a PDF, collect a drawn or typed mark, stamp it, hash it, log an IP and a timestamp. An agent will do that in an afternoon and it will work perfectly for you. It will not work for the other party, who has to open a link from a domain they have never heard of, trust that your audit log is not something you edited last night, and then rely on it if the contract is ever disputed. D4Sign sells a third party attesting to the signing event, plus ICP-Brasil qualified certificate integration, retention, and the fact that Brazilian counterparties and courts already recognise the name. Self-hosting the signer means you are both the notary and the interested party, which is the one role you cannot play.
coreLoopDIY: Upload a PDF, email a signing link to each party, capture their signature and consent, stamp the signed PDF and write an append-only audit trail you host yourself.
requirements: SMTP credentials for sending signing links
A domain and HTTPS host that counterparties will plausibly click
Somewhere durable to keep signed PDFs and audit logs for years
whatYouLose: A neutral third party vouching for the signing event, which is the entire point in a dispute
ICP-Brasil qualified certificate signing and the legal weight that comes with it
Counterparty trust: people hesitate to sign on a domain they do not recognise
Retention, redundancy and a company that still exists in seven years when the document matters
Integrations with ERPs, CRMs and the API plumbing Brazilian back offices already wire into
moatNotes: MP 2.200-2/2001 lets simple electronic signatures hold up between consenting parties, so the code is legal enough. The problem is evidentiary, not technical: your own server's log is a weak witness.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because signatures are bought for the day they are challenged, not the day they are collected. Paying a provider converts a homemade log file into third party evidence, adds qualified certificates for the documents that need them, and means the counterparty's finance team does not stall for a week asking who is hosting this link. For a solo operator signing their own NDAs, a self-hosted signer is genuinely fine. For anything with money or a regulator attached, the fee is cheaper than the argument.
notes: Build it for your own low-stakes paperwork and nothing else. The moat is not the signature capture, it is being a disinterested third party with a name Brazilian counterparties and courts already accept.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted document signing app. Stack: Next.js App Router with TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind, pdf-lib for PDF manipulation, nodemailer for email. No auth provider, no cloud storage, no telemetry.

Single admin user, password hashed with argon2, read from .env. SMTP host, user, pass and APP_URL also from .env. Provide .env.example.

Admin flow:
- Upload a PDF, give the envelope a title.
- Add one or more signers: name, email, and a page plus x/y position for their signature box, picked by clicking on a rendered preview of the PDF.
- Send. Each signer gets an email with a unique unguessable signing link (32 byte random token, single envelope, no login).

Signer flow (public, token-gated):
- Show the full PDF in a viewer, require scrolling to the end before enabling the sign button.
- Capture a signature either drawn on a canvas or typed and rendered in a script font.
- Explicit consent checkbox with plain language about electronic signing.
- On submit, record signer IP, user agent, timestamp in UTC, and the SHA-256 of the document at the time of signing.

Completion:
- When all signers have signed, stamp every signature image into the PDF at its recorded coordinates, append a final page listing each signer, their email, timestamp, IP, and hashes.
- Write every event to an append-only audit table where each row stores the SHA-256 of the previous row plus its own payload, forming a hash chain. Expose a verify endpoint that recomputes the chain and reports tampering.
- Email the finished PDF to all parties and store it on disk under ./storage.

In scope: sequential or parallel signing order, envelope expiry, resend link, voiding an envelope.
Out of scope and do not fake them: ICP-Brasil or any qualified certificate integration, timestamping authority, identity verification, SMS or biometric checks, CRM integrations.

Include a README that states plainly that this produces a simple electronic signature with a self-hosted audit trail, that the operator controls the server and is therefore not a neutral witness, and that anything requiring a qualified certificate needs a real provider.
